 ORL

 Player Stats

 Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane, Anthony Black, Franz Wagner and Wendell Carter Jr. will start Monday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Suggs, who returned from a knee injury on Friday against the Bucks, is back in the starting lineup for Monday’s game. As a result, Tristan da Silva will come off the bench. While his value takes a hit with the lineup change, da Silva is still worth holding onto since the Magic are without Paolo Banchero (ankle). The other four starters are unchanged. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  Orlando Magic

 Tristan da Silva 
 ORL 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Tristan da Silva provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (4-of-6 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, three steals and three three-pointers against the Celtics on Monday. 
 With Jalen Suggs returning to the starting unit, da Silva was pushed to the bench, though he was still able to have a productive night. He was able to set a season high for steals, which also matched his season totals, so managers shouldn’t expect that many swipes often. He’ll continue to provide offense off the bench, though his upside will be capped as a reserve. 
 Jalen Suggs 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Jalen Suggs returned to the starting lineup on Monday and contributed 12 points (5-of-8 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics. 
 Suggs came off the bench on Friday, which was his return from an eight-game absence. He came off the bench one time last year, which was also his first game back after an extended absence, but before that, he hadn’t come off the bench since his second season in the league. Suggs played just under 25 minutes and will likely remain on a minutes restriction for some time. However, as the minutes increase, the fantasy production should too.

 Tristan da Silva (calf) and Jamal Cain (shoulder) are game-time decisions for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Da Silva’s status is of far greater consequence to fantasy basketball, especially with Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs both out. At a minimum, da Silva should be rostered even after those two Magic starters return. As for Cain, despite there being more opportunities for him to contribute, he isn’t worth the risk in most redraft leagues.

 Anthony Black finished with 20 points (7-of-13 FGs), one rebound, six assists, three steals, one block and three three-pointers against the Celtics on Monday.
 It has been a strong season so far for Black, though he did struggle in their last game. However, he was able to get back on track in this one. He scored at least 20 points for the fourth time this season, with three of those coming in his last four games. Black continued to start despite Jalen Suggs moving back into the starting lineup, which bodes well for his value, at least until Paolo Banchero returns. At that point, head coach Sean Sweeney will have a tough choice between Suggs and Black.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Franz Wagner

 Player Stats

 Franz Wagner posted a full line on Monday with 21 points (8-of-21 FGs), eight rebounds, nine assists and one block against the Celtics.
 Wagner’s 30-point game streak came to an end after four straight, but he was still productive in this game. The shots didn’t fall as well, but he continued to play the role of playmaker, even with both Jalen Suggs and Anthony Black in the starting lineup, which propelled Orlando to a fourth straight win. Outside of a random game where he only had one assist, he has had at least five assists in every game this season. Now that he’s scoring better, the numbers are looking great. They should remain inflated until Paolo Banchero returns, though that could impact his usage.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Jarrett Allen recorded a double-double on Monday with 13 points (6-of-9 FGs), 14 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block against the Bulls.
 With Evan Mobley (toe) out for this one and expected to miss at least another week, Allen was able to control the paint, finishing as the game’s leading rebounder and helping Cleveland win the rebounding battle 51-37. That also matched his season high for boards. Allen continues to be a steady producer for fantasy managers, with the occasional big performance. Hopefully a boost in boards will continue, at least until Mobley returns.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Donovan Mitchell

 Donovan Mitchell led the Cavaliers with 39 points (16-of-25 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers in a 126-115 win over the Bulls on Monday.
 After getting the night off on the second leg of Cleveland’s back-to-back on Saturday, Mitchell was able to have a strong scoring performance in this one. The extra rest may have helped since he was able to set a new season high for scoring. Mitchell’s usage rate is down this season, but he has shot the ball more efficiently, except at the free throw line. That mark will certainly improve, which will help his overall value and scoring numbers. He was effective at the charity stripe in this one, making all five of his attempts.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Tyrese Proctor started on Monday and finished with 17 points (6-of-13 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers against the Bulls.
 Proctor was the lone starter from Saturday’s game that remained in that role for this one. All five starters were out for that game, and Evan Mobley remained out, while Jaylon Tyson was also sidelined after starting on Saturday. He recorded a triple-double in an extended role in that game, and while he didn’t produce to that level in this one, he still contributed a strong stat line. If Tyson misses their matchup with Memphis on Wednesday, Proctor will have streaming appeal. However, he’ll likely head back to the bench when Tyson returns.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Norman Powell led the Bulls with 27 points (10-of-18 FGs), two rebounds, six assists and one steal in a 126-115 loss to the Cavaliers on Monday.
 Apparently taking two games to rest his back did wonders for Norm. Over the last three games, he has averaged 28 points per game while shooting 57.1 percent from the floor. Powell has been a strong scoring option for Chicago all season, but he has really stepped up as of late. That scoring will be needed with Caleb Wilson set to miss at least a month. Powell will look to stay hot over the Bulls’ three remaining games this week.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Matas Buzelis lit up the Cavaliers with 23 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, one steal, one block and three three-pointers on Monday.
 It was a rough start to the season for Buzelis, but he is starting to pick the production up. This ended up being a new season high for scoring for him, and while he didn’t dish out any dimes, he made up for it with efficient shooting and some defensive production. Buzelis may not live up to preseason expectations, but he should be much better than how he started the season. Chicago will need him to if they want to turn their season around, especially with Caleb Wilson set to miss at least a month.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Tre Jones provided a boost off the bench with 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, six assists and four steals against the Cavaliers on Monday.
 Jones has been a solid source of offense off the bench for Chicago this season, which continued in this game. He was also part of the team’s closing lineup instead of Josh Giddey. That doesn’t mean Giddey is going to lose his starting spot, but head coach Tiago Splitter isn’t afraid to go with the hot hand if the starter is struggling. Still, Jones has been solid, but he shouldn’t be rostered in standard leagues unless Giddey misses time.
 -  Noah Rubin
